# Establishment log — popol-vuh-003 (images 0015–0016, end of sentence from 0019)

Read 2026-11-23 from source/pages/i0015–i0016 (and the first three lines of i0019) in strips at 1.6–2×,
checked word by word against Brasseur 1861 (OCR lines 18896–19300). Start: `Chi cutun ibi, Hunahpu Vuch`
(0015, line 3, right after `Cha ta chuxoc`). End: `xcute qui vach.` (0019, line 3); the next words,
`Cax xiban chique`, begin the speech of the dogs and turkeys/stones, which belongs to popol-vuh-004.

## Images 0017 and 0018 are blank
The stored crops i0017 and i0018 carry no writing at all (whole image checked at reduced size and in
strips). The text runs straight on from the last line of 0016 (`… qui quebal`) to the first line of 0019
(`qui xot, qui lac, qui boh …`), exactly as Brasseur prints it, so nothing is missing: these are blank
leaves (or blank captures) in the LoC image set. The part therefore ends on 0019. Folios: 0015 = 4r and
0016 = 4v follow popol-vuh-002's count; 0019 taken as 5r, on the assumption that the blank leaves are not
foliated (the folio number is outside the crop). popol-vuh-004 (parts.json: images 0018–0020) begins at
0019 line 3.

## Letter rule used (popol-vuh-002's rules, unchanged)
- q-shaped letter where Brasseur has g → ꜫ, u dropped: `vꜫihiloxic`, `Ꜫih, bit`, `ꜫih` (×3), `Ratit Ꜫih`,
  `ahꜫih` (×2, one with a blot between h and q), `Ꜫucumaꜩ`, `xe poꜫic` (B. pogic), `xꜫecumaric`
  (B. gekumaric), `ꜫecal`, `ꜫihil`. NB the pilot's house table prints `queꜫum` with plain qu at the start;
  002's rule was followed here.
- the ɛ/3-shaped tresillo → ꜫ: `ahꜫol` (B. ahgol), `nima ꜫol` (B. gol), `qui ꜫab` (first time, B. gab).
- g-shaped letter → ꜭ: `Ꜭaholom`, `qui ꜭux`, `Vꜭux Cah` (×4), `ꜭuxlaai`, `ꜭoh`, `xe ꜭaholanic`; gh → ꜭh:
  `quix vꜭhaxic`, `xe vꜭhaxic`, `xeꜭha`, `xꜭha`, `caꜭhauic`, `chi ꜭhauic`, `que ꜭhau`, `xeꜭhauic`, `Xꜭhauic`.
- plain c kept where Brasseur has q or g: `cutun` (B. qutun), `vcahic` (B. kahic), `chi cotox` / `chi ca
  cotah` (B. qotox, qotah), `cat choconic` (B. chogonic), `cacan` (B. c'akan), `qui cab` (second time) and
  `qui cabchiyal` (B. gab, gabchiyal), `qui cutuxic` (B. gutuxic), `xcotin` (B. qotin), `xcahixic` /
  `cahizabal` (B. qahixic, kahizabal), `xcut` (B. qut), `acabal hab` (B. agabal hab), `Ah Raxa Lac`
  (B. lak; the pilot printed `Laꜫ` for the same title — the image here has a plain c).
- q-shaped letter where Brasseur has q kept qu: `vinaquil`, `tiquiba`, `taquentah`, `quyzic`
  (B. qizic; the letter is g-like but followed by u, so read as qu — doubtful, see below).
- ß-ligature: ti where Brasseur has ti (`Hunahpu Vtiu`, `vtihtobexic`, `xtio`, `xticaric`, `vtiohil`,
  `ticoval`); ꜯ in tz' words (`Ꜯyꜩ` as the pilot's `Nimac Ꜯyꜩ`, `caꜯac`, `cahꜯac`, `Ahꜯac`, `Ꜯacol`); ꜩ
  otherwise (`ꜩite`, `ꜩucul`, `ꜩihon`, `Vꜩ`, `ꜩaꜩ`, `coꜩ`, `Camaloꜩ`, `Coꜩbalam`, `ꜩi`). No comma is
  visible on the ligature in `ꜩite`, so it is printed ꜩ although the word is tz'ite' (the modern toggle
  supplies tz').
- loop-t (h-like) read t: `atit`, `Ratit` ×2, `Tucumbalam` (MS looks `hucumbalam`), `xtucuuic`.

## Doubtful readings
- `pichipoh` (0016): clear in the image; Brasseur's OCR is garbled here (`Nemo`). Meaning unknown.
- `vvababexic` (0016): MS `vvaba-/bexic`; Brasseur's OCR garbled. Letters as seen; the word is uncertain.
- `ca ieioh` (0016): MS `caie-/ioh`; Brasseur `ca yeyoh`.
- `qui quyzic` (0016): see above; Brasseur `qui qizic` ('their end').
- `qui caa` (0019): the letter after qui is a c with a flourish; Brasseur prints `qui aq` here. Read
  `caa` (grindstones, which speak in the next part); uncertain.
- `xcute qui vach` (0019): MS `xcuhe`, loop-t read t; Brasseur `x-qutu qui vach`. Uncertain.
- `xbanic` (0016): the a is closed and looks like u (`xbunic`); Brasseur x-banic.
- `xtucuuic` (0016): Brasseur x-tukuvic; printed the letters as seen.
- `Cat quix la vloc` (0015): MS `quixla`, divided as Brasseur (`qix la`); a blot on the c of `vloc`.
- `ma ca hizah` (0015): MS `macahizah`; Brasseur `m'aqahizah`. Division uncertain.
- `xe pah chi vi` (0016): MS `chivi`; Brasseur `chiri`.
- `xe pe Camaloꜩ` (0016): MS `xe pe` with a singular subject, as written (Brasseur `x-e pe`).
- `Nimac, Nima Ꜯyꜩ` (0015): MS `nimac nima / ꜯyꜩ`; the pilot has `Zaqui Nimac Ꜯyꜩ`. Possibly a repetition.

## Word order and Brasseur differences, image followed
- `ahcuval` (B. ahqual); `Ahtoltecat` (B. ah-Toltecat), joined as written and capitalised as a name.
- `ri i poy` (B. ri y poy); `chavaxoc` with v (the pilot spells `chauaxoc`).
- `xmuchulixic qui baquil, cahizabal qui vach`: the MS has `qui baquil` a second time; Brasseur omits it.
- `xrah oquic` (B. xah oquic): the MS has an r.
- `qui chuch, [blot] chuvach puch` (0016): a blotted correction before chuvach; nothing legible under it.

## Paragraphs
Ximénez's paragraph mark and capital at `Cate cut qui quyzic chic` (0016), where Brasseur begins his
chapter three; the other breaks follow his full stops at the turns of the story.
